title: [AUG-217] Pin the update install folder on Windows when its path contains a space
why_we_need_this: AUG-216 makes the updater pass `/D=<folder of the running exe>` to the NSIS installer so an update can never land in another folder, but only when the folder path has no whitespace. Reason: electron-updater starts the installer through Node `spawn`, Node wraps an argument containing a space in quotes (`"/D=C:\Users\John Smith\..."`, verified 2026-11-17), and NSIS accepts only an unquoted `/D=` as the last argument; electron-builder's GetDParameter would keep the trailing quote in `$INSTDIR` (read from the template, not run). So installs in `C:\Program Files\August` (every per-machine install) or under a user name with a space still take the folder from the registry and can drift to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\August` after an interrupted update (AUG-207). Their data is found again through the data-location.json pointer, but the app then runs from a second copy and the old copy stays on disk. Users affected: everyone whose install path contains a space. Details: @project-context/desktop-shell/README.md, section "Implemented fix (AUG-216)".
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] On packaged Windows builds the installer is started with an unquoted `/D=<folder of process.execPath>` as the last part of the raw command line when that folder contains a space (for example `C:\Program Files\August`), for both the direct start and the `elevate.exe` start.
- [ ] The installer path itself (and the `elevate.exe` path) is still passed correctly when it contains a space or non-ASCII characters (for example a user profile `C:\Users\John Smith` or a Cyrillic user name).
- [ ] Folders without a space keep the current AUG-216 behaviour; `/D=` stays the last argument and `autoUpdater.disableWebInstaller` stays true.
- [ ] The command-line building is a pure function (no Electron imports) in or next to @electron/src/installLocation.ts, with unit tests for: path with a space, path without a space, Cyrillic path, installer path with a space, the elevated variant; tests run for both `win32` and `darwin` platform values.
- [ ] A local check that prints the raw command line of a harmless child process (not an installer) shows the unquoted `/D=` tail for a path with a space; its output is quoted in the task result.
- [ ] macOS and unpackaged runs are unchanged: every new branch is guarded by `process.platform === 'win32'` and `app.isPackaged`.
- [ ] `pinnedInstallDir` no longer returns null for a path with a space, and the `[updater] Install folder not pinned` log line is removed or limited to the cases that still cannot be pinned.
- [ ] `npm run electron:test`, the server tests and `npm run build` pass, and the Electron smoke test (AUGUST_SMOKE_TEST=1) prints SMOKE_OK.
- [ ] The desktop-shell route section "Implemented fix (AUG-216)" and its TL;DR lines about the whitespace limit are rewritten to the new behaviour.
important_constraints:
- Depends on: AUG-216-b3t877 (must be accepted first; this task changes its `pinnedInstallDir` rule).
- Never run installers or uninstallers against the real install (`D:\claude\August\installed`) and never touch its `data` or the registry key `HKCU\Software\8ed30dcd-7880-51a9-bc47-ea538a6afaa3`.
- No VM or second Windows profile is available (user decision 2026-11-16): unit tests, the raw-command-line check, build and smoke test are the bar. State in the result that the installer path was not exercised end to end.
- electron-updater's `spawnLog` / `doInstall` are library internals (version ^6.8.9, @node_modules/electron-updater/out/NsisUpdater.js and BaseUpdater.js): prefer the smallest override, keep the other installer arguments (`--updated`, `/S`, `--force-run`) and the EACCES → `elevate.exe` fallback, and note in the route which library version the override was written against.
- If no safe override exists, stop and report options instead of shipping a partial change: a broken installer start blocks every update for these users, which is worse than the current fallback.
- Cross-platform rules from the project CLAUDE.md apply; do not change the data-dir pointer logic or @electron/build/installer.nsh.
- The smoke test exits without SMOKE_OK while the installed August is running (single-instance lock); ask the user to quit it, never kill it.
- Commits go straight to master.

## Result (2026-11-17)
- @electron/src/installLocation.ts: `pinnedInstallDir` rejects only a `"`; new pure `quoteWindowsArg`, `verbatimInstallerSpawn`, `windowsCommandLine`.
- @electron/src/updater.ts: `pinVerbatimInstallerStart` overrides `spawnLog` on the autoUpdater instance (written against electron-updater 6.8.9). Only when the last argument is exactly `/D=<pinned folder with whitespace>` does it spawn with `windowsVerbatimArguments` and a quoted `argv0`; everything else goes to the library's spawnLog. The EACCES → elevate.exe and ENOENT fallbacks are unchanged.
- Tests: `npm run electron:test` 43/43 (win32 + darwin hosts), server 940/940, `npm run build` OK, smoke test SMOKE_OK.
- Raw command line of a harmless child (a renamed node.exe in a folder with a space and Cyrillic), read back through Win32_Process:
`"…\scratchpad\Fake Dir Влад\fake installer.exe" -e "…" -- --updated /S --force-run /D=C:\Program Files\August`
- Elevate shape (printed, not run): `"C:\Program Files\August\resources\elevate.exe" "<installer>" --updated /S --force-run /D=C:\Program Files\August`
- NOT exercised end to end: no real NSIS update, and elevate.exe was not run (needs UAC), so how it forwards the raw tail is not verified.
- Context: @project-context/desktop-shell/README.md, section "Implemented fix (AUG-216)" plus the TL;DR line.
